question: A 25-year-old previously healthy woman presents to her PCP reporting cessation of menses for the past 6 months. Previously, her period occurred regularly, every 30 days. She also complains of decreased peripheral vision, most noticeably when she is driving her car. She denies any recent sexual activity and a pregnancy test is negative. Upon further work-up, what other physical findings may be discovered?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cessation of menses" -> "possible hormonal imbalance" -> "potential pituitary adenoma" -> "decreased peripheral vision" -> "possible visual field defects" -> "possible decreased bone density" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Cessation of menses" -> "possible hypothalamic dysfunction" -> "altered estrogen levels" -> "possible bone density loss" -> "possible decreased bone density" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Cessation of menses" -> "negative pregnancy test" -> "possible endocrine disorder" -> "possible pituitary issue" -> "decreased peripheral vision" -> "possible visual field loss" -> "possible decreased bone density" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Cessation of menses" -> "negative pregnancy test" -> "possible hormonal changes" -> "possible pituitary adenoma" -> "decreased peripheral vision" -> "possible visual field defects" -> "possible breast mass" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Cessation of menses" -> "negative pregnancy test" -> "possible thyroid dysfunction" -> "possible enlarged thyroid" -> "possible hormonal imbalance" -> "possible decreased bone density" -> 65%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of amenorrhea and decreased peripheral vision suggest a possible pituitary adenoma, particularly a prolactinoma, which can lead to hyperprolactinemia and secondary amenorrhea. This condition can also cause visual field defects due to pressure on the optic chiasm. Among the options provided, decreased bone density is a plausible finding due to prolonged amenorrhea leading to estrogen deficiency, which can negatively impact bone health. Therefore, decreased bone density is the most relevant physical finding that may be discovered upon further work-up.
